strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas GH#66323 (PR#66323, buggy commit 61cbe5f9c92c) where array_equivalent/Series.equals become inconsistent for native complex dtype when NaN appears in either real or imaginary component. The reproducer uses the project’s own new regression test `test_array_equivalent_complex_nan_component` and ensures it runs against the buggy revision (fastpath complex-as-float-pairs) and passes on the fixed revision (drops that fastpath and uses whole-element complex isna semantics).

build_commands: python -m pip install -U pip setuptools wheel
pip install tzdata; true  # only needed on Windows/Emscripten
pip install .  # non-editable OK for CI; editable shown below
pinned_because: Numpy is numerically relevant (README dependency) but the evidence does not provide a documented minimum/maximum constraint; choose a reasonably recent stable numpy to ensure native complex + NaN behavior matches the bug report, and keep it the same across buggy and fixed runs.
Cython is required to build from sources per README; avoid skipping builds because array_equivalent is in core missing/compiled extensions may be exercised depending on build options.

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy revision (61cbe5f9c92c), running the test command should FAIL: `assert array_equivalent(left, right, dtype_equal=True)` is False for native complex dtype with NaN in real or imaginary part even though both elements are NA under whole-element semantics, while `dtype_equal=False` returns True (self-inconsistency). After checking out the fixed revision from PR#66323, the same test should PASS for all parametrized `dtype` values and for both `dtype_equal` settings.
strategy.numerical_probe: array_equivalent on complex arrays where either real or imaginary component is NaN (whole complex considered NA). The failing decision point is whether the implementation takes the complex-as-float-pairs fastpath for native complex dtype instead of the whole-element `np.isnan` logic.

input_output_examples.input: array_equivalent(np.array([complex(1, np.nan)], dtype=dtype), np.array([complex(2, np.nan)], dtype=dtype))
input_output_examples.expected_output: array_equivalent(...) should return True for both dtype_equal values because both elements are NA under whole-element complex semantics (either component is NaN).

risks: No explicit pandas/numpy version constraints are provided in the evidence. If the fastpath bug is version-sensitive, the transition may not occur on an environment with substantially different numpy/pandas build behavior; keep the same Python/numpy across buggy and fixed runs and use the project’s standard CI-like versions.

The bug is described for native complex dtype and includes endianness variants (`>c16`, `>c8`). Some platforms/toolchains may not exercise all variants identically; if failures only appear on little-endian (or vice versa), that would be consistent with this being architecture/toolchain dependent.

If running on environments that omit building optional extensions or change Cython/C-extension compilation flags, execution paths might differ. Use `pip install .` or editable install with build isolation disabled as provided to maximize parity with the reported behavior.

oracle.reference_source: Project regression test for GH#66160/66323 semantics, introduced in PR#66323 (`test_array_equivalent_complex_nan_component`).
oracle.why: The test asserts boolean equivalence directly (no numeric tolerances) and checks `array_equivalent` returns truthy/falsy outcomes consistent with whole-element complex NA semantics across `dtype_equal=True/False`.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assertion `assert array_equivalent(left, right, dtype_equal=dtype_equal)` fails for `dtype_equal=True` when `left=np.array([complex(1, np.nan)], dtype='c16'/'c8'/native complex variants)` and `right=np.array([complex(2, np.nan)], dtype=...)` (and similarly for NaN in the imaginary part). This happens because the buggy implementation takes the complex-as-float-pairs fastpath and compares real/imag independently, disagreeing with the dtype_equal=False path that applies whole-element NA semantics.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: After applying the PR#66323 fix (dropping the complex pair-view fastpath for native complex and using whole-element complex `np.isnan`-based logic), `array_equivalent` returns True consistently for both `dtype_equal=True` and `dtype_equal=False` for all parametrized complex dtypes in the test, so the entire test function passes.
